title: Runtime compatibility stability pledge and upgrade assistant
creator: Maya Patel
description: Define a pragmatic semantic versioning and LTS channel policy for the serving runtime that minimizes customer regressions while enabling safe, measurable improvements. Deliver an "upgrade assistant" command-line and console workflow that enables automated compatibility checks, migration steps, and preflight dry-runs for customer environments.
decisions: Adopt a three-track release model: rapid (minor feature) channel, stable (monthly) channel, and long-term-support (LTS) channel with 12-month security/backport window.
Major versions (X.y.z where X increments) reserved for breaking changes that require opt-in upgrade tooling; breaking changes must be gated and documented with migration shims where feasible.
Minor versions will allow additive features and non-breaking behavioral changes; deprecations are announced in minor releases and carried for two minor cycles before removal in the next major.
Introduce a Compat-Profile header that allows clients to declare strict/lenient compatibility expectations; servers will honor compat hints and surface compatibility warnings in responses.
Upgrade Assistant will be the canonical tool for migration testing: it runs compatibility checks, KV cache validation, model artifact schema checks, and smoke tests before scheduling a live upgrade.

All breaking or potentially disruptive changes require a gated rollout plan that includes canary percentage, automated health gates, and an automatic rollback policy if error budget exceeds threshold.
tasks: Draft formal Versioning RFC and ship to eng + product for review (DOC: confluence/runtime-versioning-pledge).
Implement Compat-Profile request header and server-side warning surface in runtime (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284).
Prototype Upgrade Assistant CLI with preflight checks and dry-run mode (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/upgrade-assistant).
Add rollout gate automation to deployment pipeline: canary orchestration and rollback hooks (infra ticket ENG-15011).
Create automated test suites that exercise deprecation windows across multiple minor versions and LTS backports.
acceptance_criteria: RFC approved by Release Engineering and API owners.
Compat-Profile header implemented and integration-tested end-to-end.
Upgrade Assistant can run preflight checks against a staging cluster and produce a deterministic compatibility report.
Deployment pipeline enforces rollout gates and will auto-stop/rollback if error budget > 2% during canary.
Documentation published in Console docs and Confluence with migration recipes and timeline examples.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: internal dogfooding for two weeks on dedicated infra with 5% of traffic routed via canary profile.
Stage 2: opt-in public beta for early adopters with manual approval and Upgrade Assistant guidance.
Stage 3: gradual promotion to stable channel contingent on metrics; LTS releases follow stable after three stable cycles.
Each canary must run Upgrade Assistant preflight; if incompatibility score > 0, block promotion and open follow-up ENG ticket.
lts_policy: LTS releases occur annually and are supported for 12 months for bug fixes and security backports.
Critical bug/security fixes may be cherry-picked into the last two stable minors for users who do not adopt LTS.
Customers can opt into extended support contracts for multi-year LTS maintenance (commercial offering).
deprecation_policy: Deprecation notices are announced at least two minor release cycles before removal.
Deprecations must include migration guidance, Upgrade Assistant checks, and telemetry that flags usage of deprecated APIs.
Telemetry for deprecated feature usage is retained for 6 months to prioritize migration assistance and sample converts.
api_compat_rules: Backward compatibility is required for request/response schema and default semantics within a minor series.
Behavioral changes that may affect output tokens (formatting, kv cache semantics) are considered breaking unless gated by feature flags and opt-in headers.
Introduce deprecation headers (Deprecation-Date, Deprecation-Info) in responses to notify clients programmatically.
upgrade_tooling_spec: Upgrade Assistant features: compatibility-report, dry-run, auto-migrate (best-effort), and rollback-simulation.
CLI integrates with Console to upload preflight snapshots and visualize diffs between current and target runtime versions.
Tooling will emit machine-readable reports (JSON) and human summaries; reports include failed checks categorized by severity.
monitoring_and_gates: Primary SLOs to watch: 99th percentile latency, error rate, and token success rate.
Canary gating thresholds: error rate delta < 0.5% and latency regression < 10% relative to baseline; breach triggers immediate rollback.
Expose rollout metrics in Console with per-route breakdown and a compatibility health dashboard for upgrade windows.
rollback_plan: Immediate automatic rollback if canary error budget exceeded.
Retain previous model and runtime artifacts for 72 hours post-upgrade to accelerate fallback.
Post-rollback incident review to identify migration failure causes and document required tooling fixes.
